question: In 1965, two astronauts reported to Mission Control that they'd spotted something like Santa in orbit. Then they pulled out a smuggled harmonica and bells and played the first song ever performed in space. Which song?
source_excerpt: Sixty years ago, when instruments were played in space for the first time, it was Jingle Bells all the way

extra.why_interesting: Players think of space music as something grand or scientific. The first live performance up there was a cheeky sleigh-ride tune on a pocket harmonica, after a fake 'UFO sighting' prank on Mission Control.
extra.verification_notes: Gemini 6A's Schirra and Stafford played Jingle Bells on harmonica and bells on Dec 16, 1965, after the Santa 'UFO' report; Smithsonian and Guinness agree.

explanation: The Gemini 6 crew snuck the harmonica and bells aboard, and both instruments are now kept at the Smithsonian.

question: When Silent Night was first sung in a village church in Austria, the organ wasn't used. Instead, the young priest who wrote the words accompanied the singers himself. What instrument did he play?
source_excerpt: Joseph Mohr took the tenor part and played guitar, while Franz Xaver Gruber sang bass.

extra.why_interesting: Everyone pictures the most solemn church carol sung with a grand organ. It actually debuted with a humble folk instrument played by the priest himself.
extra.verification_notes: Mohr sang tenor and played guitar at the 1818 premiere per stillenacht.at; the organ-damage reason is disputed but the question doesn't depend on it.

explanation: Franz Gruber set Joseph Mohr's poem for two voices and guitar, an instrument many people at the time thought belonged in taverns rather than churches.

question: Forget Elvis, the Beatles and Elton John. According to Guinness World Records, the best-selling single of all time is a Christmas song sung by Bing Crosby. Which one?
alternative_answers: I'm Dreaming of a White Christmas
source_excerpt: is considered to be the best-selling physical single of all time with an estimated 50 million copies sold.

extra.why_interesting: Players assume the all-time single sales record belongs to a pop or rock megahit like Elvis, the Beatles or Elton John. It actually belongs to a gentle 1940s crooner's Christmas ballad.
extra.verification_notes: Guinness World Records lists Bing Crosby's 'White Christmas' as the best-selling physical single of all time (~50 million), and no newer record has displaced it.

explanation: Crosby's recording has sold an estimated 50 million copies. It was written by Irving Berlin, a Jewish immigrant who grew up without celebrating Christmas.

question: True or false: Mariah Carey's All I Want for Christmas Is You went to number one on the US Billboard Hot 100 in the year it came out.
topic: All I Want for Christmas Is You
source_excerpt: first reached No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 on the chart dated December 21, 2019

extra.why_interesting: The song is so dominant that everyone assumes it was a number-one smash on release. In fact, chart rules kept it off the Hot 100 for years, and it only reached the top a quarter-century later.
extra.verification_notes: The song was released in 1994 but did not top the Hot 100 until December 2019, so 'False' is correct (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_I_Want_for_Christmas_Is_You).

explanation: False. It wasn't sold as a US single at first, so it couldn't chart, and it finally hit number one in 2019, a full 25 years after release.
